text:
acme_infra: Hey team — running into a 403 when our compliance team tries to view audit logs. Worked yesterday, now getting 'forbidden'. Can you help?

maria (Support): Sorry you're blocked — can you paste the exact curl and the error body? Also, which org/tenant id?

acme_infra: Org ID 0123456789. Curl:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi..." "https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/orgs/0123456789/audit/logs?start=2026-03-10T00:00:00Z"
```
Response:
```json
{
  "status": 403,
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "entitlement_missing: audit_logs_read"
}
```

maria (Support): thanks — that error is helpful. Two quick possibilities: 1) token doesn't have audit scope, or 2) org-level entitlement for audit_read/retention isn't granted. Did you recently switch SSO/SCIM or change the billing plan?

acme_infra: We did upgrade to enterprise plan yesterday and migrated SSO from Okta to a new IdP last night. SCIM sync shows groups ok. No config changes on your console that we did.

maria (Support): ok. can you run an introspect or paste the decoded token payload (redact PII)? We just need the scp/scope claims and the org claim. You can use jwt.io or:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://auth.redwood.example.com/introspect" -d "token=eyJhbGciOi..."
```

acme_infra: introspect output (redacted):
```json
{
  "active": true,
  "sub": "user:alice@acme.com",
  "org": "0123456789",
  "scp": "openid profile email",
  "exp": 1764213476
}
```

maria (Support): aha — scp does NOT include audit:read. That explains the 403 with entitlement_missing. Likely the IdP/consent didn't include the audit scope. Two remediation paths:
- Quick: create a short-lived API key with audit_read for the user/org (if allowed by policy) so compliance team can pull logs while we fix SSO.
- Permanent: update OIDC client scopes/consent or SCIM mapping to include audit:read scope on token issuance, or map an IdP group to the internal role that has audit entitlements.

acme_infra: We were relying on group->role mapping (SCIM). SCIM shows group 'Compliance' mapped to role 'audit_reader' in your console. But token still missing scope.

jake (Infra Eng): quick note — scope claims are produced by the auth server at token mint. If you use OIDC code flow with offline access, the ID token might not include custom scp until the client is configured to request them. SCIM group mapping affects account entitlements in our system (backend), but the runtime API also checks token scopes. There are two checks: token-level scopes AND org entitlement flags. Both must pass.

erin (Security): adding: sometimes after SCIM migration the entitlement sync job lags. We should verify the org entitlement for audit_logs_read is true. @jake can you run an entitlement check for org 0123456789?

jake (Infra Eng): starting entitlement check now. running internal tool:
```bash
/internal/tools/ent-check --org 0123456789 --feature audit_logs_read --output json
```

ops-bot: job 5c9f started by jake (Infra Eng) at 2026-03-15T14:17:05Z

jake (Infra Eng): result: {"org": "0123456789", "feature": "audit_logs_read", "granted": false, "source": "scim-sync", "last_synced": "2026-03-15T03:12:11Z"} — appears SCIM mapping did not flip the entitlement on our side.

maria (Support): ok that aligns with the API error. Two concurrent issues: token lacks audit:read scope AND our entitlement flag wasn't set. For a quick unblock I can grant a temporary entitlement while you fix IdP config. Need approval from security. @erin?

erin (Security): i'm fine with a temporary grant for 24h for compliance pulls, provided we log the action and require audit for the grant itself. jake — can you apply a 24h grant and log?

jake (Infra Eng): will apply with TTL. running:
```bash
/internal/tools/ent-grant --org 0123456789 --feature audit_logs_read --actor maria.support --ttl 24h --reason "customer emergency: audit access blocked after SSO migration"
```

ops-bot: entitlement-grant request queued (req id = eg-7a2). Approvers required: erin (Security).

erin (Security): approved.

ops-bot: entitlement eg-7a2 applied: audit_logs_read=true for org 0123456789 (expires 2026-03-16T14:18:20Z). Action logged under sec-audit-2026-03-15.

maria (Support): OK acme_infra — I applied a temporary entitlement. Can you retry the same curl now? If you still get 403, we'll fix the token scope next.

acme_infra: retrying... Response now 401 with message 'token_missing_scope: audit:read' — so entitlement is set but token still missing scope as suspected.

maria (Support): perfect — that confirms both checks are live. For the token fix: either mint a new token that requests audit:read scope, or update the IdP/OIDC client so issued tokens include the scope. Which flow are you using (auth code, service account, SAML assertion)?

acme_infra: we use SAML SSO to get SAML assertion -> exchange to get long-lived API token via our internal automation. The automation expects certain claims and then calls our token-exchange endpoint. We didn't include audit scope in the exchange anymore after the IdP change.

maria (Support): path forward: 1) update automation to request audit:read during token-exchange; 2) optionally create a scoped API key in Redwood console for the compliance group. If you want I can generate a scoped API key with 'audit:read' scoped to org 0123456789 and set expiry. That avoids touching IdP right now.

acme_infra: let's do the scoped API key for now. We'll change automation after.

maria (Support): creating a scoped key with 7d expiry now. Generating...

ops-bot: api-key-create request queued (req id = key-9b3).

jake (Infra Eng): note for longer term: after you change automation, ensure the token exchange endpoint requests the 'audit:read' scope and that the IdP's client allows it. On Okta/GCP OIDC you'd add the scope to the client's allowed scopes and add claim mapping if needed.

ops-bot: api-key key-9b3 created for org 0123456789, scope=[audit:read], expires=2026-03-22T14:25:05Z. Key value redacted in log.

maria (Support): key is in the console under org settings > API Keys. I'm DMing the key to your org contact alice@acme.com now. Please rotate/delete once automation is updated.

acme_infra: received key, pulling logs now — success, we're able to query range back to retention window. thanks so much.

maria (Support): great. final notes:
- root cause: SCIM sync didn't flip org entitlement + IdP token issuance didn't include audit:read scope after SSO migration.
- short-term fix: temporary entitlement + scoped API key for compliance.
- long-term: update IdP/OIDC client to allow audit:read and update automation to request it; also confirm SCIM mapping and run a full entitlement resync.

jake (Infra Eng): i'll trigger a full scim->entitlement resync for org 0123456789 and add a monitoring alert if last_synced > 12h without change.

erin (Security): will review policy for granting entitlements during onboarding and add a checklist for SSO migrations.

maria (Support): i'll follow up with a short postmortem and steps for your team to avoid this during future IdP migrations. closing this thread when you confirm automation updated. :thumbsup:

acme_infra: will confirm once automation updated. thanks again!
